items.title: Daily TCGplayer price history — Sync Prices records the day
items.body: Price history from TCGplayer, driven by the **existing Sync Prices button** — not a second control. The CLI, the `.bat`, and Task Scheduler stay available for unattended runs. Verified against live TCGplayer and a real Postgres. ## What you click In Binder Vault: - **Sync Prices** / **Refresh All** (page toolbar) — today's Near Mint prices for the open page, recorded as daily history - **Backfill 1 yr History** (Ledger, under "Prices as of …") — the one-time year pull There is no separate "Update Prices" button. Sync Prices now calls the same `@vip/pricing` sync as the job, so a page that already has values still writes today's history instead of no-oping. [Ledger with Backfill only — no Update Prices button](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-697f2faa-8e5d-4fa7-a2a3-ddbfa9019666/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fbinder-ledger-no-update-prices.webp) ## Verified this turn Live POST to `/api/binders/b-test/sync-prices` on the already-priced Price Test binder (Charizard $852.42 ×2, Pikachu $15.60, one manual slot): | Field | Result | |---|---| | slotsChecked / skipped | 3 / 1 (manual) | | historyRowsNew / historyRowsUpdated | 0 / 60 | | table row count | stayed **156** (idempotent) | | newestObservedOn | 2026-08-16 | | slot as-of | stayed Aug 16 — no regression | Browser toast after clicking Sync Prices: `Synced prices — 3 updated, 0 unchanged · through 2026-08-16` The `+N history day(s)` clause is omitted when the day is already stored, which is the second-click case. [Sync Prices toast through 2026-08-16](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-697f2faa-8e5d-4fa7-a2a3-ddbfa9019666/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fbinder-sync-prices-toast.webp) Earlier live run (empty history → first fill): Charizard $852.42, Pikachu $15.60, total $1,720.44. Annual backfill toast said "through 2026-08-10" but the as-of line stayed Aug 16 — the do-not-regress guard. ## One implementation, three entry points The sync core lives in `@vip/pricing` behind an injected `SqlRunner`, so Sync Prices, `npm run job:price-history`, and the daily scheduler share it. The package takes no driver dependency; each caller passes its own pool. ## The useful discovery The TCGplayer endpoint Binder already called returns much more than one number. Measured live: | `range` | Granularity | Span | |---|---|---| | default | **1 day** | ~30 days | | `quarter` | 3 days | ~87 days | | `annual` | 7 days | ~1 year | Each bucket carries market price, low/high sale price, quantity sold, transaction count, and date — **segmented by condition and printing**. So history doesn't start empty: one backfill gives a year. Confirmed 78 distinct NM days per card (2025-08-18 → 2026-08-16) after a daily run plus one backfill. **NM is selected, not assumed.** TCGplayer reports NM / LP / MP / HP / Damaged separately, so the job filters for Near Mint and only falls back when a card has no NM row — flagging `condition_assumed` with unverified provenance. ## Rule 4 TCGplayer publishes a market price **even on zero-sale days** — only 7 of 30 days had transactions for the test card. Days with trades are `observed`; quiet days are `normalized · unverified`. A valuation can then weight real sales instead of treating a model output as a trade. This needed a `markNormalized` helper; the provenance schema already allowed the method but had none. ## Two bugs the testing caught Both silent data corruption, found only by running it: - **A `--condition=LP` run overwrote the collection's value** — the binder slot went $852.42 (NM) → $509.72 (LP), a ~40% undervaluation from what should be a read-only query. Slots now only accept NM. - **The annual backfill moved freshness stamps backwards**, making freshly priced cards look stale. Both retested; the SQL guards are now asserted in unit tests, not just observed. ## Schema note I did **not** reuse `vault_tcg.price_snapshot`. It is keyed on `slot_id` with `ON DELETE CASCADE`, so rearranging a binder page would have destroyed price history, and a card in two binders would store it twice at double the API cost. New `vault_market.card_price_history` is keyed on `(source, external_id)` — card-grained, so history outlives layout. `price_snapshot` is left in place (nothing ever wrote to it) and marked superseded. ## Still available for unattended runs ```powershell npm run job:price-history -- --backfill=annual powershell -File scripts\schedule_price_history.ps1 # daily 06:00 task ``` ## Limits - Only `source = 'pokemontcg'` cards with an external id; manual slots are skipped and counted. - Sports cards need the catalog work in ADR 0010. - Unofficial endpoint, so parsing is pinned to a captured real response and adapters are swappable (rule 5). - The `.ps1` parses under a real PowerShell parser with no 7.x-only syntax, but I can't run Windows Task Scheduler from here — that registration is unverified on your machine. CI is green (TypeScript + Python ingest). ## PR note (VIP DoD) - **User:** owner who wants current values and a price history without a second Binder button or a terminal - **Decision:** TCGplayer at NM as price source of truth; one shared sync behind Sync Prices, CLI, and schedule; history card-grained, daily, idempotent, and honest about trades vs model output - **Input evidence:** live payload with per-condition daily buckets, sale ranges and transaction counts - **Output action:** Sync Prices / Refresh All / Backfill writing `vault_market.card_price_history`, with binder values updated only by NM and never backwards To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

items.title: Security: Harden database lifecycle, type-safe rejection handling, and patch dependencies
items.body:
Why

The faucet contained untyped rejection handling, swallowed shutdown-cleanup failures, unsafe database lifecycle transitions, and detached PoW worker shutdowns.  Test scripts relied on Unix-only commands, and the dependency tree contained a vulnerable transitive package (brace-expansion).  

How

Typed unhandled rejections securely using unknown and guarded stack access with an explicit Error check.  Ensured database initialization is idempotent and partial state/workers are properly reset on failure.  Awaited delayed session cleanups and PoW server shutdowns to prevent cross-lifecycle race conditions.  Replaced Unix-only test copy commands with cross-platform Node.js helpers.  Added root overrides to secure vulnerable transitive dependencies.  

Security changes
Prevents unhandled runtime exceptions, data corruption, and silent cleanup failures.  Mitigates supply-chain risks by cleaning up vulnerable dependency paths.  

Testing
Verified npm run build and npm audit pass with zero high-severity vulnerabilities.  Confirmed cross-platform test execution succeeds seamlessly.

items.title: boot: embed build-id and DWARF debug info in PE binaries

labels.name: please-review
labels.description: PR is ready for (re-)review by a maintainer

items.body:
systemd-boot EFI binaries created by elf2efi.py had no debug info. Change it so that build-id and DWARF sections are transferred from intermediate ELF to final PE binaries. DWARF, as usual, is enabled by buildtype=debug, disabled by buildtype=plain and overwritten by custom CFLAGS -g.

This enables distributions to strip symbols from systemd-boot PE files, archive them in .build-id/xx/yyyy.debug and enable automatic symbol discovery by gdb:

```sh
build_id=$(objdump -p systemd-bootx64.efi | sed -n 's/.*RSDS signature \([0-9a-f]*\).*/\1/p')
mkdir -p ".build-id/${build_id:0:2}"
objcopy --only-keep-debug systemd-bootx64.efi ".build-id/${build_id:0:2}/${build_id:2}.debug"
objcopy --strip-debug systemd-bootx64.efi

(gdb) file systemd-bootx64.efi
```

As a further benefit, the embedded build-id can be used as a fingerprint to search for in target memory and calculate the load address of systemd-boot after it was loaded and relocated by UEFI.

The [ELF build-id](https://sourceware.org/gdb/current/onlinedocs/gdb.html/Separate-Debug-Files.html) is transformed according to binutils BFD equality check (see bfd/peXXigen.c, `_bfd_XXi_slurp_codeview_record`) and stored as PE's [CodeView GUID](https://github.com/microsoft/microsoft-pdb/blob/master/include/cvinfo.h). DWARF sections are looked up by names listed in the [DWARF spec](https://dwarfstd.org/doc/DWARF5.pdf) and are copied byte-wise since they're never SHF_ALLOC and don't need relocation handling.

items.title: A structural insert or delete moves the tables too
items.body:
**FID-22, a verified P0 — silent data corruption.** Inserting or deleting rows and columns never moved a table.

## What it was

`structural.rs` shifted merges, the sheet's `auto_filter`, `filter_hidden`, sizing, hidden lines, the freeze boundary and outline levels on every structural edit — and **`sheet.tables` appeared nowhere in the file.** The only `tables.iter_mut()` calls in the entire workspace were the table operations themselves.

So inserting one row above a table left its range, banding, filter buttons and column list on the old row numbers. `SUM(Table1[Amount])` then read the header text row and dropped the last record: **a wrong number in a saved file, with no error and nothing in the compatibility report.**

The module's own header comment lists what has to move "or a merge, custom height, or freeze silently" breaks. Tables were never added to that list, or to its tests.

Found by the `docs/73` UX parity audit and confirmed against the source before any code changed.

## The fix

**In the trait, not at the call sites.** `Positional` gains `tables_mut`, so `Sheet` and `SheetMetadata` both get it from the one macro — the bundle needs the same shift when a pending metadata edit is rebased past someone else's insert (ADR-011), and a shift implemented twice is a shift that disagrees with itself the first time a field is added.

A table's range moves exactly like a merge. Its **own** `auto_filter` range moves with it, because a table filters independently of the sheet and leaving that behind puts the filter buttons on the wrong columns.

A delete clamps the range, drops the table when the band takes all of it, and removes the `TableColumn` entries **by position** — keyed by where each column *was*, because when the deleted band only partly overlaps the table the survivors are the ones outside it, not the first or last N.

**Widening sideways mints a column as well as the room for it.** `columns` is indexed left to right and every structured reference resolves through it, so a range one wider than the list silently shifts every column's meaning by one. Ids stay unique because a filter rule names a column by id, and the generated `Column{n}` name is checked against the existing ones because two columns sharing a name make `Table[Column2]` ambiguous. Only an insert **strictly inside** widens — one at the table's own first column pushes the whole table right instead, which is what `at > start` distinguishes.

## Evidence

Five gates: a table moved wholly down, a table grown from the inside, a column insert that must produce a matching `TableColumn` with a unique id and name, a column delete that must keep the survivors outside the band, and a table deleted out of existence.

**Mutation-verified:** removing the table handling from both paths fails all five — the first with the table still on rows 3..6 where it should be on 5..8.

794 tests pass outside the collab-server crate; clippy, fmt and doc clean; fuzz workspace checked. The server crate is untouched by this change.

**Left open and recorded:** `header_row_count` and `totals_row_count` are not adjusted when a delete removes the header or totals row itself.

items.title: refactor: key coordinator storage by CredentialAddress

labels.name: python
labels.description: Pull requests that update Python code

labels.name: code-quality
labels.description: Pull requests that improve code quality

items.body:
## Proposed change

Flips the coordinator's internal storage from `dict[int, SlotCredential]` to `dict[CredentialAddress, SlotCredential]`, with `_unverified` following. This is what lets one slot hold more than one credential type — the capability the user-centric model needs.

Follows #1415, which introduced `CredentialAddress` and re-signed the coordinator's *accessors*. This one moves the *storage* behind them.

**Behavior is unchanged.** `user_ref` is still the slot number and the type is still Personal Identification Number, so every key is `(n, PIN)`.

**Boundaries deliberately keep their slot-keyed shape:**

- The **websocket payload** and **diagnostics output** are contracts with things outside this integration — the dashboard card reads one, and people paste the other into issue reports. Both now go through a new `credentials_by_slot()` projection. Lossless while PIN is the only stored type; the wire format re-keys later, shipping with the card.
- **`providers/_base.py::_pending_writes` is now address-keyed too.** An earlier revision of this PR left it slot-keyed and claimed that was correct permanently. Code review disproved that: once one slot holds two credential types, `_apply_read` iterates both `(5, PIN)` and `(5, RFID)`, both index `_pending_writes[5]`, and whichever is processed first consumes and deletes the entry — applying the pending PIN's believed value to the wrong credential, and leaving the second silently marked verified. The first is data corruption. Fixed in `7f9fae7c`.

That scoping is why this PR touches no TypeScript and needs no card change.

**New read accessors:** `credential(address)`, `has_credential(address)`, `credentials_by_slot(type)`. `credential()` returns `None` for "never reported", which stays distinct from `SlotCredential.empty()` — a positive observation that the slot holds no code.

## Type of change

- [ ] Dependency upgrade
- [ ] Bugfix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- [ ] New feature (which adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix/feature causing existing functionality to break)
- [x] Code quality improvements to existing code or addition of tests

## Additional information

- Full suite: **1494 passed, 3 skipped** (baseline 1492 on main)
- Coverage: **100.00%**, unchanged
- `ruff check`, `ruff format`, `pydocstyle`, `flake8`, `mypy`: all pass

Most of the test diff is mechanical — `coordinator.data[1]` becomes `coordinator.data[pin_address(1)]`, and iteration goes through `credentials_by_slot()`. Seeds via `async_set_updated_data` needed the same treatment, since they bypass `_normalize_keys`.

One test is not mechanical and is the point of the PR: `credentials_by_slot`'s type filter never excludes anything today, because every stored credential is a PIN. Line coverage therefore cannot pin it, so a test seeds a non-PIN address directly to prove the websocket and diagnostics boundaries will not start emitting an RFID value under a PIN slot key once a second type is stored.

items.title: Versioned schema migrations for authdb (replace CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS blobs)
items.body:
## Problem

The schema is applied as two idempotent DDL blobs at open time: `migrate()` (`internal/authdb/authdb.go:64`) creates `users`, `api_keys`, `compiles`; `migrateOAuth()` (`internal/authdb/oauth.go:87`) creates `oauth_clients`, `oauth_authorize_sessions`, `oauth_authorization_codes`, `pdf_links`. Both are `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` only, run unconditionally from `Open()` (`internal/authdb/authdb.go:44-57`).

This works for a greenfield database and for adding a brand-new table, and nothing else:

- **No `ALTER` path.** `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` is a no-op against an existing table, so adding, renaming, or retyping a column on a deployed database silently does nothing. The code would expect a column the live DB does not have.
- **No applied-state record.** Nothing distinguishes a fresh database from one three revisions behind. There is no way to tell, on a running pod, which schema version the file actually is.
- **No ordering.** The two functions are sequenced only by their call order in `Open()`. As soon as a change spans both, correctness depends on an implicit convention rather than a declared sequence.
- **No failure isolation.** Each blob is one `Exec`; a partial failure part-way through leaves the schema in an undefined state with no record of how far it got.

This matters more than it would in most projects because the data is not reconstructible: `api_keys` stores sha256 hashes only, so a botched migration cannot be recovered by re-deriving keys. Every user would have to re-authenticate.

**#40 is the forcing function.** It needs `users.quota_per_day` added by `ALTER`, plus new `invites` and `admin_audit` tables — the first real schema evolution this project has faced, and precisely what the current approach cannot express. Land this first.

## Decisions

- **A failed migration aborts startup.** The step rolls back, `Open()` returns an error, and the process exits rather than serving against a half-applied schema. In practice that means a crashlooping pod, which is the correct failure mode when the alternative is silent data corruption.
- **A newer-than-expected database refuses to start.** If the file is at a higher revision than the binary knows about — the image-rollback case — exit with a clear error naming both revisions. An old binary against a new schema is undefined behaviour: it may read columns that moved or write rows that violate constraints it has never heard of. The cost is accepted: rolling back an image crashloops until you roll forward or restore a backup.

## Scope

- A `schema_version` table (or `PRAGMA user_version`) recording the applied revision.
- An ordered list of migration steps, each with an explicit revision number and description, replacing the two DDL blobs. Existing DDL becomes revision 1 so current deployments adopt it without a rewrite.
- Each step runs in a transaction; failure rolls back that step and aborts startup with an error naming the revision that failed.
- Migrations run once at `Open()` and are a no-op when already current.
- Baseline detection: an existing pre-versioning database (tables present, no `schema_version` row) is stamped at revision 1 rather than re-running DDL or failing.
- Downgrade guard as decided above.
- Document how to add a migration, and note in `DEPLOYMENT.md` that the state volume should be backed up before upgrading to a version carrying one.

## Out of scope

Adopting a migration framework or a backend-as-a-service (PocketBase et al.). Evaluated and declined: PocketBase cannot act as an OAuth 2.1 authorization server for third-party MCP clients ([discussion #7451](https://github.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/discussions/7451)), which is the part of `internal/auth` that is hardest to replace, and it remains pre-1.0 with no backward-compatibility guarantee — an awkward property for the component holding unrecoverable key hashes.

Also out of scope: `compiles.user_id` is `TEXT` (`"gh:42"`) while `api_keys.user_id` is `INTEGER` referencing `users(id)`, so `compiles` has no foreign key and accumulates rows for deleted users. Noted as a known inconsistency; reconciling it is a follow-up that would ride on this mechanism. (#40 handles the orphan rows directly by deleting them on user delete.)

## Test plan

**Core mechanism**
- [ ] Fresh database opens, runs all migrations, reports the current revision
- [ ] Opening an already-current database is a no-op and does not error
- [ ] Opening twice in a row leaves the revision unchanged (idempotent)
- [ ] Migrations apply in revision order, not declaration or map-iteration order
- [ ] An added test-only migration (e.g. `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN`) actually applies to an existing database — the case the current code cannot do

**Baseline and compatibility**
- [ ] A pre-versioning database (tables present, no `schema_version`) is stamped at revision 1, existing rows intact
- [ ] All seven existing tables and their constraints match the pre-change schema after migrating from empty
- [ ] Existing `authdb` and `pdflinks` tests pass unchanged

**Failure handling**
- [ ] A step that fails mid-way rolls back and leaves the recorded revision at its previous value
- [ ] A failing migration aborts `Open()` with an error rather than returning a usable `Store`
- [ ] The error names the revision that failed
- [ ] A database at a higher revision than the binary supports is refused, with both revisions in the message

**Operational**
- [ ] Manual: copy the test-overlay `auth.sqlite`, open with the new binary, confirm stamped at revision 1 with users and keys intact
- [ ] Manual: confirm an existing API key still authenticates after the upgrade (no re-auth required)
- [ ] Docs: process for adding a migration is written down; `DEPLOYMENT.md` notes the backup step

items.title: fix(host): fix the project lease and install lock for non-admin Windows users
items.body:
## Goal

Add same-user isolation coverage for the project lease (`MutexProjectLease`), the last gap the 2026-08-15 audit found in P8.34-P8.41. Implementing it surfaced and fixed a real production defect in the primitive under test.

## What shipped (final state)

- **New `tests/Forge.MutexIsolationProbe`**: exercises the real production `MutexProjectLease.TryAcquire`.
- **`.github/scripts/test-same-user-isolation.ps1`**: extended with a same-user contention sanity check and a cross-user denial check for the mutex, mirroring the existing pipe check's shape (`CurrentUserOnly` restricts a security descriptor on one shared object — it does not namespace per user, so a different user is *denied*, not handed an independent object).
- **`src/Forge.Host.Client/ProjectLease.cs`** / **`src/Forge.Runtime/Providers/ProviderInstallLock.cs`**: `NamedWaitHandleOptions.CurrentSessionOnly` is now chosen per platform via `OperatingSystem.IsWindows()` — `true` (session-scoped) on Windows, `false` (`Global\`, the strongest guarantee) everywhere else. Windows previously always used `Global\` unconditionally, which requires `SeCreateGlobalPrivilege` — a privilege standard non-admin users don't hold by default, so their Host process failed outright at startup every time. Non-Windows platforms keep the stronger guarantee unchanged, since they never had this privilege problem.
- **`tests/Forge.Tests/Unit/ArchitectureTests.cs`**: a static test pinning `ProjectLease.cs`'s and `ProviderInstallLock.cs`'s two independent copies of this construction identical, so they can't silently diverge.
- **ADR 0005 / `CHANGELOG.md` / the plan note**: document the final mechanism and all three rejected intermediate designs (always-`Global\`, a per-process capability probe, uniform session-scoping) and why each was wrong.

## Design history (why this took several iterations)

This went through 6 independent review rounds (3 full-scope + 3 critical-only), each catching a real defect in the previous fix:
1. Always `Global\` → fails outright for non-admin Windows users (the original bug).
2. Catch-and-fallback on the real lease name → ambiguous between "I lack privilege" and "a different user already holds this lease," silently handing a genuinely contending user an independent object.
3. Capability determined once via a dedicated probe → reflects the *process token* (UAC elevation), not the account, so the same user's elevated/non-elevated processes stopped excluding each other.
4. Uniform session-scoping everywhere → fixed that, but unnecessarily weakened Unix, which never had a privilege problem with `Global\`.
5. **Final: platform-conditional** (`OperatingSystem.IsWindows()`) → keeps the strongest guarantee wherever the OS actually allows it.

## Verification

- `dotnet build`/`dotnet test` — clean, 473 + 551 passing on Windows; Linux/macOS portable-core run (`test-portable.ps1`) genuinely exercises `ProjectLeaseTests`/`ProviderInstallLockTests` including the `Global\` construction path, 473/473 passing.
- `lint.ps1`, `Stage0.Contracts.Tests.ps1`, `test-stage1.ps1`, `test-portable.ps1` — all passed.
- `same-user-isolation` CI job (creates a genuine second Windows local user) — green, log confirms both the pipe and mutex isolation assertions.
- All 7 CI checks green on the final commit.

## New version

`0.28.1` (PATCH — this is a `fix`, not a `feat`).

## Compatibility impact

None breaking. Behavior fix: the project lease and provider-install lock now work for standard non-admin Windows users (previously they did not work at all). Windows session-scoping does not extend across two concurrent sessions of the same user (e.g. console + a simultaneous RDP session) — a disclosed, accepted trade-off.

## Release notes

See `CHANGELOG.md` under `## v0.28.1`.

## Related

Closes the 2026-08-15 architecture audit backlog (final item, task #45 of that backlog).

items.title: [Bug]: Allwinner A64 / sun50i-a64 (Pine64) - Hardware Crypto Engine (`sun8i-ce`) corrupts OpenSSH key exchanges and RSA host key generation

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Something isn't working as it should

items.body:
### What happened?

### Summary
Allwinner A64 / sun50i-a64 (Pine64) - Hardware Crypto Engine (`sun8i-ce`) corrupts OpenSSH key exchanges and RSA host key generation

### Board / OS Details
- **Board:** Pine64 (Allwinner A64 / sun50i-a64)
- **Architecture:** aarch64 (sunxi64)
- **Kernel Branch:** Current (Linux 6.x)
- **Target OS:** Ubuntu Noble / Debian Trixie (Armbian Current)

### Description
On modern Armbian images for the Pine64 (sun50i-a64), the Allwinner hardware crypto engine driver (`sun8i_ce` / `CONFIG_CRYPTO_DEV_SUN8I_CE`) causes silent data corruption during cryptographic operations. 

Because OpenSSH 9.x+ utilizes crypto offloading for key exchange (KEX), SHA hashing, and signature validation, incoming SSH sessions fail immediately during handshake or authentication with errors such as:
- `ssh_dispatch_run_fatal: Connection to <IP> port 22: message authentication code incorrect`
- `ssh_dispatch_run_fatal: Connection to <IP> port 22: incorrect signature`
- `accumulate_host_timing_secret: encode ssh-rsa key: unexpected internal error` (preventing sshd restart on corrupted host keys)

### Root Cause Analysis
The A64 silicon has known errata/defects in its CE (Crypto Engine) hardware implementation for SHA hashing and certain cipher routines. When `sun8i_ce` is loaded, kernel crypto API routes operations to the hardware instead of standard ARMv8 NEON/CPU software implementations, poisoning OpenSSH handshakes and host key generation.

### Verified Workarounds / Fixes
Disabling the driver completely resolves all connection drops and allows standard SSH to function normally:

1. **Kernel Config:** Set `CONFIG_CRYPTO_DEV_SUN8I_CE=n` for `sunxi64` family kernels, or default it to modular blacklist.
2. **Boot Argument:** Passing `extraargs=initcall_blacklist=sun8i_ce_init modprobe.blacklist=sun8i_ce,sun8i-ce` in `armbianEnv.txt`.
3. **Device Tree:** Setting the crypto block to disabled in `sun50i-a64-pine64.dts`:
   ```dts
   &crypto {
       status = "disabled";
   };

### How to reproduce?

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Flash a fresh Armbian image (Noble/Bookworm, `sunxi64-current`) to an SD card for Pine64.
2. Boot headless and attempt to connect via SSH (`ssh root@<IP>` or standard user).
3. The connection drops during key exchange or public key verification with `incorrect signature` or `message authentication code incorrect`.

### On which OS are you observing this problem? (for easier diagnosis please provide logs with `armbianmonitor -u`)

items.title: Build Add Artist flow
items.body:
Part of #646.

## Scope

Search box → `MusicBrainzService.SearchArtists` (#649) → result list → user picks one → get-or-create composition, run **client-side**, exactly ADR 0026's 3-step pattern:

1. `ExternalIDService.GetExternalIDByValue(entity_type=LIBRARY_ENTRY, source=mbz, value=mbid)` (#647). Hit → navigate to the existing artist, done.
2. Miss → `LibraryEntryService.CreateLibraryEntry(kind="artist", content_type="music", name, sort_name, metadata: {artist_type, aliases, founded_date/dissolved_date or born_date/died_date, isni, official_url, wikipedia_url})` — fields populated from the `MusicBrainzArtist` DTO exactly per ADR 0021's reuse table, no invented fields.
3. `ExternalIDService.CreateExternalID(entity_type=LIBRARY_ENTRY, entity_id=<step-2 id>, source=mbz, value=mbid)`. Response `entity_id` differs from step 2's id → this call lost the race → `DeleteLibraryEntry(<step-2 id>)`, navigate to the winner instead. Matches → done, navigate to the new artist.

Also, best-effort: call `TheAudioDBService.LookupArtist(mbid)` (existing RPC) and write `Genre`/`Style` into `Metadata["genre"]`/`["style"]` if TheAudioDB has a match — a miss does not fail the flow, those keys are simply left unset. This is what #664's grid chip reads.

**Explicitly not built here:** creating/linking the solo-artist `Person` record ADR 0021 describes ("solo artists get two records") — that is #672, a separate story. This flow creates the `LibraryEntry` only.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Integration test exercises a concurrent-duplicate-add (two callers importing the same MBID at once) and asserts exactly one `LibraryEntry` exists for that MBID afterward, per ADR 0026's guarantee — this is the one place in this epic where getting the race handling wrong is silent data corruption, so it's tested explicitly, not left to code review.
- The TheAudioDB genre/style lookup's hit and miss paths are both covered by test.
- Depends on #649, #647, and the existing `LibraryEntryService.CreateLibraryEntry`/`ExternalIDService.CreateExternalID`/`TheAudioDBService.LookupArtist` RPCs.

## Governing ADRs

0021 (music domain model — exact field mapping), 0026 (external-ID get-or-create — the composition pattern), 0027 (provider independence — TheAudioDB passthrough), 0020 (server-generated IDs).
